text:
jordan: seeing sustained throughput drop on a subset of dedicated workers, started ~10:12 UTC after the runtime deploy. P50 fine, p95/p99 and overall qps down ~30%. Logs show repeated worker restarts and some OOMs.

maria: noted, can you paste the first OOM log? also is this across all regions or one pool?

jordan: one pool (dedicated-us-west-2-pool-4). Recent logs:
```
[2026-03-18T10:15:02Z] ERROR worker=worker-42 pid=789: cudaOutOfMemory: allocation failed size=1.28GB slab_id=3
[2026-03-18T10:15:05Z] INFO supervisor: restarting worker-42 (crash_count=3)
```

kai: infra-bot alerted on allocator churn earlier, I pulled `perf` on the affected pod. Kernel selection is oscillating between fast-path int8 kernels and fallback fp16 kernels which changes memory pressure; vm stats show slab fragmentation. sample from `kmem` counters: `slab_free_frag=0.18 -> 0.05` over 30m.

infra-bot: [alert] 2223334444 - worker_restart_rate high on dedicated-us-west-2-pool-4 (3.8/min)

oncall-bot: Pager duty assigned to @maria (oncall)

maria: thanks. hypothesis: new heuristics we shipped for kernel_pref (aggressive selection based on perf_estimate) causes higher peak allocation for certain sequence-length mixes -> more fragmentation -> OOM + restarts. Also saw increased KV cache eviction activity in same window.

leo: quick mitigation: can we pin kernel selection to `stable_v1` and ramp the batching caps down? quick test suggested: set `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096` and `KERNEL_MODE=stable_v1`.

maria: I prepared a tiny canary patch, disabling the new kernel predictor and lowering concurrent batches for the pool. deploy command:
```
kubectl -n serving set env deploy/worker-serve-dedicated KERNEL_MODE=stable_v1 BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096
kubectl -n serving rollout restart deploy/worker-serve-dedicated --selector=pool=dedicated-us-west-2-pool-4
```

kai: profiling after canary (10m window): restarts dropped from 3.8/min -> 0.4/min, p99 latency reduced 18%, qps recovered ~22% on canary nodes. Kernel switch rate metric: `kernel_switches/s` dropped 72%.

jordan: nice, can confirm with traffic routed to canary pool we don't hit the eviction spike. however when the canary has long-running sessions we still saw intermittent KV cache thrash: `kvcache.evictions/sec` went up briefly when BATCH_MAX_TOKENS lowered.

eva: that makes sense — smaller batches reduce prefix reuse and increase unique KV keys touched, causing higher eviction churn. short-term we can increase `kvcache_retention_ms` for that pool and bump `evict_threshold` a bit to avoid premature evictions. I suggest `KVCACHE_RET_MS=900000` and `KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESH=0.72` as a canary.

leo: agreed. applied via configmap update and a rolling restart for the pool.

maria: after both mitigations (pin kernel + kv tweaks) the pool stabilized. summary metrics post-change (30m):
- qps: +25% vs incident baseline
- p99 latency: -20%
- worker restarts: -90%
- kvcache.evictions/sec: -60%

kai: root cause writeup draft: the new kernel predictor occasionally overestimates memory headroom for mixed-length workloads, selecting kernels with higher intermediate allocation patterns. This increased slab fragmentation under our CUDA allocator variant; combined with sudden reduction in prefix reuse (due to batching shift) the KV cache started thrashing, amplifying allocation pressure and triggering OOMs and restarts.

jordan: good summary. next actions:
- (maria) revert kernel predictor flag in next minor release and add safety cap on predicted allocation (ETA: today)
- (kai) implement smoothing in kernel selection decisions (debounce switches to avoid oscillation) and add per-pool memory headroom monitoring (ETA: 2d)
- (eva) tune default KV cache eviction policy and add metric-driven auto-retain for pools with high prefix variance (ETA: 3d)
- (leo) add canary automation to run the above combo for 1 hour on 5% of traffic before global rollout (ETA: 1d)

oncall-bot: incident status: mitigated. keep monitoring for 6h.

maria: I'll follow up with a short postmortem and include the profiling artifacts and command snippets. good catch everyone :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks all — keeping this thread open for the postmortem link and any follow-ups.
